entries.reason: no HEALTHCHECK: the toolbox image is a short-lived CI job container, not a service, so a health check has no consumer
the <details><summary> line is Markdown for the GitHub job summary, which GitHub sanitizes; every interpolated value goes through cell(), which escapes < as <, so text from a log cannot open a tag
<owner> and <reason> are placeholders in a plain-text hook deny message shown in the CLI; nothing is rendered as HTML
<reason> is a placeholder in plain-text lint gaps printed to the terminal; nothing is rendered as HTML
human:<id> is a placeholder in a plain-text lint gap printed to the terminal; nothing is rendered as HTML
<producer>/<version> and human:<id> are placeholders in plain-text docs-lint warnings printed to the terminal; nothing is rendered as HTML
the literal <orbit> in a node:test assertion message names the token the test forbids; it goes to the test output, nothing is rendered as HTML
<sha> is a placeholder in a plain-text proof gap printed to the terminal; nothing is rendered as HTML
<number>, <step>, <file>, <type> and <area: ...> are placeholders in gh CLI command lines printed for the owner to fill in; nothing is rendered as HTML
test inputs: <<EOF here-documents and an <x@example.com> trailer in shell command strings fed to the guard under test; nothing is rendered as HTML
the RegExp is the test's reference implementation; heading comes only from the test's fixed list ["Steps", "Exit tests"], never from input, so no attacker controls the pattern
merges a scenario's expect object, read from the plugin's own scenarios/<name>.json, over a fresh object of defaults for a local test comparison; no user or request input, no web response
